headlines.title: San Jose officer hurt during traffic stop that prompted police shooting
headlines.description: A San Jose police officer was injured during a traffic stop that prompted another officer to shoot their gun, authorities said. The incident was reported 2:54 a.m. Monday when police stopped a vehicle in the area of North 21st and Santa Clara streets. San Jose police said the traffic stop “led to an officer getting injured and a second officer discharging a firearm.” The suspect vehicle then sped off. Police said a possible suspect vehicle was found in the area of Lucretia Avenue and Tully Road. The officer’s injuries are considered non-life threatening, police said. No other information was immediately available. San Jose 4 hours ago San Jose 23 hours ago San Jose Oct 17 Woman detained while walking on Hwy. 101 in San Jose dies

headlines.title: Justice Department carries out California sweep targeting alleged noncitizen voters
headlines.description: Federal authorities charged more than two dozen foreign nationals Monday in California as part of a statewide sweep targeting people who officials say have illegally registered and voted in U.S. elections. The arrests are part of a Trump administration effort to root out noncitizen voting ahead of next month’s midterm elections, even though data shows that the problem is incredibly rare, difficult to prove and has not been shown to change the outcome of races. They also reflect a further escalation in a simmering voter roll fight between the federal government and California that came into focus last week when the Justice Department sued the state and later warned that local election workers who knowingly process or tabulate ballots submitted by noncitizen voters are at risk of investigation and potential prosecution. The Justice Department said the 28 people who were charged as part of a sweep dubbed Operation Protect the Vote are lawful permanent residents — but not U.S. citizens who are permitted to legally vote. They are charged with crimes including making false statements on a naturalization application and submitting fraudulent voter registrations. “This causes real damage to real elections and real damage to American citizens,” Trent McCotter, the acting deputy attorney general at the Justice Department, said during a news conference in Los Angeles to announce the charges. Elections Sep 17 Decision 2026 Oct 2 California emerges as a flashpoint for voting dispute The federal government has made noncitizen voting a priority this year, demanding detailed voter information — including dates of birth, addresses, driver’s license numbers and partial Social Security numbers — from the states. While some states voluntarily handed over the information, the department sued 30 states and the District of Columbia to obtain it — lawsuits that so far have been unsuccessful. The Justice Department said Monday it has charged 113 people in 20 states with illegal voting and illegal registration offenses over the last several weeks, It earlier said it had charged about 90 people for various types of election misconduct so far this year, including 50 who are alleged to have voted as noncitizens. There were more than 227 million registered voters in the United States during the 2024 presidential election. The operation Monday involved the four U.S. attorneys’ offices across California in what the Justice Department intended as a statewide show of force. Among the dozens of people arrested was a 72-year-old Belize-born man who is accused of voting illegally in four elections. Dozens of federal agents descended on the man’s residential cul-de-sac in Commerce, a small city in Los Angeles County, to make the arrest. The man was put in handcuffs in his pajamas and taken into federal custody downtown. Others emerged from the house to watch and questioned the number of heavily armed officers present for the arrest, as well as the need for handcuffs. The arrests were the latest in a flurry of activity that has unfolded in heavily Democratic California, which is not typically regarded as a key battleground state but does have a handful of competitive congressional races that could help determine which party controls the U.S. House for the final two years of President Donald Trump’s term. Over 23 million people are registered statewide. The administration last week sued California to prevent it from counting mail ballots from people the federal government has identified as “likely” noncitizens until their immigration status can be confirmed. The complaint was filed after California officials were given, and did not meet, a 48-hour deadline to review a password-protected thumb drive that contained a list of 20,000 names. The federal government says those are likely noncitizens who were sent ballots to participate in the Nov. 3 election, although the secretary of state said the administration has provided no evidence to support that claim. The state mails ballots to all registered voters. McCotter said the 20,000 number was likely to rise. “That’s just the floor,” he said. As part of its lawsuit, the Justice Department filed paperwork Monday seeking a court order that would force California to set aside ballots from suspected noncitizens and to independently, or in conjunction with the federal government, verify their citizenship status before tabulating their mail-in ballot. The Justice Department asked for the order to be entered in time for the Nov. 3 election. Absent that order, the government said, “there is a significant risk that American votes will be diluted.” Requests for comment sent Monday to the secretary of state, state attorney general and governor’s office were not immediately returned. A warning for poll workers On Friday, the Justice Department followed up with a letter warning that state election officials who knowingly process ballots cast by noncitizen voters are at risk of investigation. “The legal consequences for either facilitating or ignoring a federal crime are significant. Noncitizen voting in a federal election is a federal crime — and knowingly facilitating such conduct is equally unlawful,” warns the letter from McCotter. It adds: “If persons knowingly tabulate ballots cast by individuals identified by federal agencies as noncitizens, they risk becoming aiders and abettors to a federal crime.” The letter is addressed to the Los Angeles County Counsel’s office and also is copied to California Secretary of State Shirley Weber and Los Angeles County Registrar Dean Logan, effectively putting the entire state on notice. In response to the letter, Logan said his office is focused on conducting a fair and secure election while noting that Election Day is a mere 18 days away. “The U.S. Department of Justice has chosen to litigate their unverified assertions of voting eligibility. At this point, it is best for this to be addressed in court,” he said. ___ Associated Press writer Eric Tucker contributed to this report from Washington.

headlines.title: Elderly couple accused of killing son-in-law in Dublin plead not guilty
headlines.description: An elderly couple accused in the killing of their son-in-law in Dublin last month pleaded not guilty Monday to charges of first-degree murder with special circumstances of lying in wait. Shili Chen and Shouyong Zhang, both 77, allegedly shot their son-in-law, 40-year-old Jonathan McKinsey, to death on Sept. 26 in the parking lot of a sports complex in Dublin. Curtis Briggs, an attorney for Chen, said McKinsey was at the complex for a supervised visit with his children, who he shared with his estranged wife Candice Jang. Briggs claims Chen did not premeditate the alleged crime but rather saw something that made her and Zhang concerned about the safety of their grandchildren and forced them to act. Briggs did not elaborate. Briggs did say McKinsey allegedly threatened to kill Chen at least three times, including once with a hitman. McKinsey, a gaming engineer for The New York Times, and Jang were in the midst of a bitter divorce and child custody dispute, both accusing the other of physical and emotional abuse. Investigators said Chen had a gun on her when she was arrested. They said they found a second gun in the couple’s car. Briggs said the couple purchased the guns in March for their own protection against McKinsey. A bail hearing was set for Nov. 4, followed by a pre-trial hearing on Nov. 23. Dublin Oct 1 Dublin Sep 30 Couple accused of lying in wait before killing son-in-law at Dublin park

headlines.title: Testimony set to continue in Sheng Thao corruption trial
headlines.description: Testimony in the corruption trial of former Oakland Mayor Sheng Thao is scheduled to resume Monday morning. Thao is on trial on allegations she offered future contracts with a waste recycling company in exchange that the men behind that company help her get elected mayor. Monday will mark the second day of testimony in the trial. Defense attorneys are expected to continue their cross-examination of Thao’s former chief of staff, Leigh Hanson. Some of the questioning of Hanson has centered around a trip Thao took to Vietnam in 2023, soon after taking office. Hanson said Thao believed the Port of Oakland covered her expenses, but prosecutors argued the majority of that trip was covered by co-defendants, David and Andy Duong, who own California Waste Solutions, which is Oakland’s recycling contractor. Hanson said she had tried to dissuade Thao from taking the trip because of the bad optics of a new mayor traveling to Asia while the city was facing serious budget issues. Sheng Thao Oct 15 Sheng Thao Oct 14 Sheng Thao Oct 13 During cross-examination last week, Hanson testified that Thao did not intervene to put people in power who prosecutors allege had been backed by the Duongs. Thao, her longtime boyfriend Andre Jones, and the Duongs have been indicted on charges of bribery, conspiracy and wire fraud. They have all pleaded not guilty. Meanwhile, during a scheduled news conference outside federal court Monday morning, the leaders behind the recall effort of Thao will not only ask for the end of no-bid contracts, but demand, in their words, accountability for corruption and an end to the political machine controlling Oakland City Hall.

headlines.title: Engine failure may have caused small plane to crash in San Jose
headlines.description: Engine failure may have caused a small plane to crash on one of San Jose’s busiest streets on Saturday, according to air traffic control recordings. Two adults and a child were in the plane when it went down at the intersection of Capitol Expressway and Excalibur Drive. They did not suffer any life-threatening injuries, the San Jose Fire Department said. Air traffic control recordings indicate the pilot was in trouble before the crash. “We are having engine failure,” the pilot could be heard saying. “I’m declaring an emergency.” The Cessna 177 aircraft was based at Reid-Hillview Airport in East San Jose and was part of a flight club linked to San Jose State University. In a statement, the university said, “The aircraft involved is owned and operated by Flying20, an independent flying club. While Flying20’s membership includes some San Jose State University alumni, employees and students, the club is not operated by the university.” The vice president of the flight club declined to comment about the crash. Neighbors said this was not the first time a plane flying out of Reid-Hillview has crashed near their homes. Maria Reyes has lived near the airport for 54 years and said she wants Reid-Hillview to close to protect her neighborhood. “We live with the constant fear of another airplane flying into our community and crashing,” she said. “People don’t seem to understand that that’s an anxiety that we live with day in and day out. We don’t know if there’s going to be another crash.” The fire department said it responded to another plane crash at Reid-Hillview Friday night. No one was hurt. The FAA said it’s investigating. NBC Bay Area reached out to the NTSB but did not immediately receive a response.

headlines.title: Valkyries fans flock to San Francisco ‘Boohalla' house to see Halloween decor
headlines.description: Lately, in San Francisco’s Inner Richmond neighborhood, you’ll find people walking, biking, and driving up to see a home near Clement Street and Third Avenue. The Halloween decorations outside the home have been adapted in great detail to reflect the season and lore of the Golden State Valkyries. As the Valkyries continue their historic stretch – playing in the WNBA finals in only their second season as a team – the people behind the display continue to make it more elaborate. The couple who live in the home, Ainsley Rossitto and Sarah Swig, are loyal Valkyries fans who moved into the neighborhood this year. The idea began as they started to plan out Halloween decorations this fall. “It really did start as a bad pun of ‘Boohalla,’ a play on ‘Ballhalla,'” explained Rossitto. “And it started to spiral when we thought, ‘Let’s dress up the skeletons.'” “Ballhalla” is what the Valkyries and their fans affectionately call their home court at Chase Center. Now, the Inner Richmond home is referred to as “Boohalla” and has social media pages. “We have really had the yard evolve, and what the skeletons are doing evolve as they are succeeding in the playoffs,” Rossitto said. “When we beat the [Dallas] Wings, [the skeletons] were out there having a chicken wing fest. When we beat the [Las Vegas] Aces, they were doing Vegas-style bottle service to celebrate,” she continued. The display is packed with Valkyries inside jokes and team references. One skeleton named “Natalie Nacauldron” is dressed similarly to the Valkyries’ head coach, Natalie Nakase. Other skeletons are giving piggyback rides, just as guard Veronica Burton has been known to do for her teammate Kaitlyn Chen. In honor of the Valkyries playing the Atlanta Dream in the finals, the yard now has an “Atlanta’s Worst Nightmare” section where a skeleton is sleeping in Steph Curry’s signature “Night Night” pose in a bed labeled Hotel Valkatraz. “We were just trying to have fun with the Valkyries’ journey with our skeletons and to kind of re-enact and celebrate the journey,” Rossitto said. “But people have been embracing us and sharing on social media. We’ve crowdsourced some ideas that people had.” At first, Swig and Rossitto said their visitors were mostly people walking through the neighborhood. But as word started to spread, they’ve met people who’ve traveled from other parts of the Bay Area just to see the display and snap photos. “We came down from Santa Rosa,” said Christina Lindh, who dropped by the display on Sunday. “We wanted to see it because this is the joy we need to see in the world right now.” After years of some big changes in Bay Area sports teams, many fans said they’re hungry for the chance to embrace this new team. “Losing the A’s, losing the Raiders,” Jaylin Kerkvliet of Santa Rosa explained. “Now, it feels like this is something that has kind of returned to form about what makes the Bay so special.” Swig and Rossitto said they have met people of all ages through their Valkyries decorations recently, some of whom have brought items to add to the display. “This ended up obviously being so exciting to everyone locally and kind of a destination,” Swig said. “I feel like we will probably do this every year.” At “Boohalla,” there are two cardboard tombstones covered in the logos of the WNBA teams that have been eliminated so far this season. Swig and Rossitto are really hoping to add the Atlanta Dream to that list. “I feel like for [the Valkyries], it’s sort of destiny – not to count our chickens before they hatch – but it will be a really, really special moment if they can pull it off,” Swig continued. The Valkyries will play Game 2 of the WNBA Finals on Monday at Chase Center in San Francisco.

headlines.title: Gilroy to vote on extending data center development moratorium
headlines.description: The future of data centers in Gilroy will be on the line Monday. There is currently a temporary moratorium on data center development in the South Bay city after community members pushed back over concerns surrounding water, power, noise and transparency. City staff on Monday are expected to recommend that the council extend the moratorium for 10 months and 15 days. Many community members say they were not given the opportunity to weigh in on any projects, and they point to the $2 billion Amazon Web Services data center that’s already under construction. That facility would not be impacted by Monday’s decision as it’s going up on 56 acres zoned for heavy industrial. A lot of community members have been voicing concerns about data center development, as has been the case in other Bay Area communities. Monday’s City Council meeting starts at 6 p.m. Community members who want to weigh in can attend in person or online.

headlines.title: Bay Area voter guide: What to know about the November 2026 election
headlines.description: What to Know — Election Day is Nov. 3, 2026 California will choose a new governor to replace Gavin Newsom, who terms out after this year. The choices are Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton. Voters will decide 14 state propositions. Regional sales tax Measure RTM, the Connect Bay Area Transit Initiative, aims to increase funds for public transit. California’s Congressional District 11 race features Scott Wiener and Connie Chan competing to succeed Nancy Pelosi. Aisha Wahab and Melissa Hernandez will face off again after a special election in August where Wahab secured victory to serve the remainder of former California U.S. Rep. Eric Swalwell’s term. All 80 California Assembly seats are up for reelection, as well as 20 Senate seats. California’s general election is Nov. 3, with statewide races and propositions as well as key local races and measures across the Bay Area. Here’s what you need to know to cast your ballot, including important dates and deadlines, how to register or check your status, where and when to vote, and what’s on the ballot. In this guide: Key election dates Check voter registration status How to register to vote How to find your polling place What to bring to your polling place How to track your mail-in ballot Why is California choosing a new governor? 14 California propositions What to watch Alameda County What to watch Contra Costa County What to watch Napa County What to watch San Francisco What to watch San Mateo County What to watch Santa Clara County What to watch Solano County County election offices Key election dates The last day to register to vote for the Nov. 3 general election is Oct. 19. County election officials will start mailing ballots by Oct. 5. Ballot drop-off locations open on Oct. 6 Last day to register to vote for the general election is Oct. 19. First vote centers open for early in-person voting in all Voter’s Choice Act counties on Oct. 24. In person early voting locations in the state open on Oct. 31. Election Day, Nov. 3, is the last day to vote in-person or return a ballot by 8 p.m. Polls will be open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. Vote-by-mail ballots must be postmarked no later than Nov. 3. If mailing on election day, get a hand-stamped postmark from a postal employee inside a post office. Visit the California Secretary of State’s website for a full list of key dates and deadlines. Check voter registration status Voters can check their registration at voterstatus.sos.ca.gov to confirm their mailing address and voting status. How to register to vote California residents can register to vote in elections at registertovote.ca.gov. Note Oct. 19 is the last day to register for the general election. Same day voter registration window will be open from Oct. 20 up to the Nov. 3 election day. Visit caearlyvoting.sos.ca.gov for a list of early voting locations to complete same day registration. How to find your polling place Visit the California Secretary of State’s website, where you can input your address to find your polling location and see what is on your ballot. Voters can also visit their county elections office for more information. Scroll down to the Bay Area county election offices section of this guide for further contact information. What to bring to your polling place Voters usually are not required to show identification to a polling place worker before casting a ballot, according to the Secretary of State’s website. There are some instances when providing identification is required: Voting for the first time after registering to vote by mail and did not provide a driver license number California identification number or the last four digits of social security number are missing on registration form In these cases voters should plan to bring identification to a polling place or bring a copy of it with their vote-by-mail ballot. The Secretary of State says the following are acceptable forms of identification: Passport Driver license Official state identification card Student identification card Copy of recent utility bill Sample ballot booklet received from county elections office Any document received by a government agency How to track your mail-in ballot Voters can track their vote-by-mail ballot and confirm it has been received by using the state’s Where’s My Ballot? tool at california.ballottrax.net/voter/. Ballots mailed in may take a few days to appear on the website. Why is California choosing a new governor? Gov. Gavin Newsom terms out after this year and voters will choose between Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton, who both advanced to the general election after a wild primary. Becerra has served as former President Joe Biden’s top health official and oversaw the response to the coronavirus pandemic. He was also the California’s attorney general during President Donald Trump’s first term and has more than two decades of experience as a congressmember. Hilton was a conservative commentator with a show on Fox News for six years. He also worked as an adviser to former British prime minister David Cameron. What are the 14 California propositions voters will decide in the November election? Here’s a list of the California propositions on the November ballot. Use the expandable graphic below for a breakdown on what to know about each measure. 2026 California Ballot Propositions Click on a proposition to see more information about what will happen if it does or doesn’t pass. Source: NBC Staff Reports • Interactive: Annetta Stogniew Regional measure to watch Measure RTM: The Connect Bay Area Transit Initiative, is a regional sales tax aimed at increasing funds for public transit. It includes 5 Bay Area counties: Alameda, Contra Costa, San Francisco, San Mateo, and Santa Clara. Races and measures to watch in Alameda County California Congressional District 14: California lawmaker Aisha Wahab and Bay Area Rapid Transit Director Melissa Hernandez will face off again to determine who will serve the next full two-year term. Wahab topped Hernandez in an August special election to serve the remainder of former California U.S. Rep. Eric Swalwell’s term. Swalwell resigned from Congress earlier this year after sexual assault and misconduct allegations. District 14 includes the East Bay cities such as Fremont, Hayward and Livermore. Measure X in Berkeley: Would establish 10% limit on annual rent increases and other changes to the city’s rent ordinance. Measure Y in Berkeley: Parcel tax to pay for arts projects. Measure Z in Berkeley: Parcel tax to fund a public bank. Measure AA in Berkeley: Increase soda tax Measure EE in Oakland: Shift city to a strong mayor system. Measure FF in Oakland: Eliminate foreclosure exemption from property transfer tax. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Alameda County and additional election information, visit the Alameda County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Contra Costa County In Contra Costa County, several county board of education seats are open. In Richmond, residents will vote on a new mayor while voters in San Pablo will weigh in on Measure S, which would limit rent increases. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Contra Costa County and additional election information, visit the Contra Costa County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Napa County California Congressional District 4: Mike Thompson faces Eric Jones. Measure B in Napa County: Sales tax to fund wildfire prevention and open space preservation. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Napa County and additional election information, visit the Napa County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in San Francisco San Francisco voters will weigh in on several open seats on the county board of supervisors and board of education. Proposition A: Give mayor more power to hire and fire department heads. Proposition B: Pave way for public bank. Proposition C: Increase the city’s annual contribution to an affordable housing trust fund. Proposition D: New barriers to placing measures on the ballot. Proposition E: Changes to city contracting. Proposition G: Reopen parts of the Great Highway to vehicle traffic on weekdays. Proposition H: Parcel tax to fund Muni. Proposition J: Eliminate foreclosure exemption from property transfer tax California Congressional District 11: Scott Wiener and Connie Chan compete to succeed Nancy Pelosi. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in San Francisco and additional election information, visit the San Francisco Department of Elections website. Races and measures to watch in San Mateo County Measure E in Redwood City: Limit rent increases. Measure Q in Half Moon Bay: Referendum to block proposed farmworker housing. Measure U in San Mateo County: Create independent commission to draw supervisor districts. For a complete list of San Mateo County measures and races on the ballot, visit smacre.gov/elections. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in San Mateo County and additional election information, visit the San Mateo County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Santa Clara County In San Jose, incumbents Peter Ortiz and Bien Doan are up for re-election in Districts 5 and 7, respectively, and there’s an open seat in District 9. Races and measures to watch in Solano County Solano County Board of Supervisors, District 4: Mike Silva and John Carli face in a runoff in a district covering Vacaville and Dixon. Measure E in Solano County: New tax on data centers and battery storage facilities in the unincorporated county areas. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Solano County and additional election information, visit the Solano County Registrar of Voters website. Races and measures to watch in Sonoma County California Congressional District 1: Mike McGuire will face James Gallagher in a seat redistricted by Proposition 50. California Congressional District 4: Mike Thompson faces Eric Jones. State Assembly District 12: Eric Lucan and Jackie Elward compete in a battle between business and labor. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Sonoma County and additional election information, visit the Sonoma County Registrar of Voters website. headlines.title: Steph Curry avoids injury scare after hobbling out of Warriors open practice
headlines.description: SAN FRANCISCO – Warriors superstar Steph Curry avoided a serious injury scare Sunday that had thousands of fans holding their breath at Chase Center. Sunday was the Warriors’ open practice, where fans flock to get a look at their favorite players in a relaxed environment. The Warriors went a little more intense than in years past but still kept it light. About 45 minutes in, there was a heaviness of a dark cloud hovering over the court when Curry limped his way to the locker room. Curry went to make a move on De’Anthony Melton when his sneakers squeaked and his body got stuck. He tapped Melton, bounced the ball hard twice and favored his right leg limping to the sidelines. Curry caught his breath and then kept limping down the hallway and to the Warriors’ locker room. The main concern was that Curry, 38, injured the same right knee that held him out for more than two months last season. Luckily for Curry and the Warriors, that doesn’t appear to be the case. Curry has a sprained right ankle, per the Warriors, and did not injure his knee. “He said he’s fine,” Warriors coach Steve Kerr said after practice. Kerr shared that he spoke with Curry in the training room and that he was in good spirits. No further diagnosis has been shared, nor has a conversation with the Warriors’ medical staff. Like everybody in the building, Kerr certainly was worried for the worst when he first saw Curry in discomfort and admitted his heart skipped a beat. “Always, always,” Kerr said. “He’s fine. I went and talked to him after he went downstairs, and I went in the training room. He’s doing fine.” The Warriors have been cautious in Curry’s ramp-up leading to Wednesday’s regular-season opener in Los Angeles against the Los Angeles Lakers. Less is more in making sure Curry is as healthy as possible entering his 18th season. He has scrimmaged less and has been part of fewer and fewer higher-intensity portions of practice. Curry played a little under 18 minutes per game in the preseason and averaged 13 points while shooting 44 percent from the field (20 of 45) and 41.9 percent from three (13 of 31). Gui Santos was on the floor when Curry came up short, but his fear wasn’t at an all-time high because of his teammate’s reaction. “Of course we were scared,” Santos said. “But it’s Steph. He’s tough. He’s going to be good. Tomorrow he’s going to wake up and be good. We were definitely worried. … The way that I saw him walking off the court, I didn’t think it was something really bad.” The Warriors already are being tested from a plethora of health problems. Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody continue to rehab leg injuries, and an illness has kept Kristaps Porziņģis away from the team for the last three weeks. Curry wasn’t the only concern from Sunday’s open practice, too. Brandin Podziemski and Charles Bassey did not participate. Bassey was seen having his right knee wrapped in ice, and the Warriors are saying he’s dealing with right knee tendinitis. Kerr did not know why Podziemski was absent but did confirm he practiced prior to the open session. Now, it’s another game of wait and see on Curry’s health days before the regular season begins. headlines.title: 1 dead and 1 arrested following crash in Oakland
headlines.description: A person was arrested on suspicion of DUI following a fatal crash in Oakland Sunday afternoon, the California Highway Patrol said. CHP said a Toyota Camry and a Honda sedan crashed on westbound Highway 24, just where it turns into the I-980, east of the 27th Street off-ramp. Authorities said the driver of the Honda was pronounced dead at the scene, and the driver of the Toyota suffered minor injuries and was arrested on suspicion of driving under the influence (DUI). The crash prompted three westbound lanes of I-980 to be blocked for hours.

headlines.title: Anthropic commits 5% of its stock to a new ‘public benefit' fund
headlines.description: Anthropic said Sunday it is committing 5% of its shares to a new “public benefit” fund, with the fund’s worth potentially increasing as its shares grow in value. The shares will go to the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, a new entity within the company. The fund “will have increased flexibility and scale, enabling us to pursue our mission in new ways: for example, we might explore large donations to traditional nonprofits or direct distributions to specific populations,” Anthropic said in a blog post. It gave labor market impacts as an example, saying that while it has already committed $200 million to study the effects of artificial intelligence, “given the pace of AI progress, bolder approaches may be needed.” CEO Dario Amodei and the company’s five other cofounders established Anthropic as a public benefit corporation, a designation that for-profit companies select to balance financial goals and social impact. They have also pledged that they will donate 80% of their wealth. An equity donation match program, in which about half of the company’s employees participate, lets workers pledge equity that Anthropic matches. When combined with Sunday’s announcement, Anthropic said roughly 20% of its shares will be dedicated to the “public good,” plus any additional percentage that could be added if the company’s valuation reaches specific milestones. Anthropic is planning a massive initial public offering as soon as November.

headlines.title: Small plane crashes into San Jose traffic; no serious injuries
headlines.description: A small plane carrying three people nosedived into traffic on one of San Jose’s busiest streets Saturday afternoon, leaving everyone aboard and on the ground with only non-life-threatening injuries. The crash occurred just before 3:10 p.m. at the intersection of Capitol Expressway and Excalibur Drive, blocking traffic, causing a minor fuel spill that crews quickly absorbed, and forced the Alum Rock Avenue off-ramp from Highway 680 to briefly shut down. Emergency responders from the San Jose Fire Department confirmed that two adults and a child were inside the aircraft — identified by Federal Aviation Administration records as a 1968 Cessna 177A Cardinal — when it went down, ending up nose-down and tail-up in the middle of the road. The three occupants were transported to a hospital out of an abundance of caution. No vehicles or individuals on the ground were struck or injured. Witnesses in the neighborhood expressed shock at finding a plane crash-landed just yards away from their homes. “It’s a close call, it’s a close call,” said Ricardo Barlaan of San Jose. Andrew Vasquez, another witness, recalled hearing the impact. Describing the moment, he made a crashing sound and said, “Boom.” “It’s crazy, I’m flabbergasted,” Vasquez said. “At first I thought it was some kind of stunt or they were making a movie or something.” Joe Lopez, who has lived in the neighborhood for 60 years, noted that while there have been past incidents involving aircraft flying out of nearby Reid-Hillview Airport, he had never seen a plane come down this close to his house. “It’s a good thing the navigator landed where he did,” Lopez said. The plane’s tail number indicates it is registered to Flying Twenty Inc., a nonprofit flight club for San Jose State University students, alumni, and faculty. According to the club’s website, they operate out of Reid-Hillview Airport. A club member reached by phone declined to comment about the organization, the pilot or what happened. It took about three hours before the wreckage was cleared from the intersection, carried away on a flatbed truck with a police escort — leaving a crumpled reminder of a crash that started with a mayday and ended with what emergency personnel called a miraculous survival story. Saturday’s incident highlights ongoing local safety concerns, marking the latest in a series of off-airport aircraft accidents tied to facilities in East San Jose. According to National Transportation Safety Board records and published news reports, several similar off-airport crashes have occurred over the decades: Feb. 24, 2002: A Piper PA-24-250 lost engine power due to fuel exhaustion while approaching Reid-Hillview Airport, forcing the pilot to make an emergency street landing about two miles away where it collided with a car. The NTSB attributed the crash to inadequate flight planning and improper fuel-consumption calculations. No injuries were reported. Nov. 19, 2017: CBS reported that a Cessna 172P suffered a partial engine power loss after taking off from Reid-Hillview Airport, crashing into a garage on Evelyn Avenue roughly 300 yards northwest of the property. While no one inside the residence was hurt, the pilot sustained minor injuries and two passengers suffered serious injuries. June 29: A small experimental gyrocopter with two people on board crashed just outside Reid-Hillview Airport near Eastridge Mall. One occupant was hospitalized with moderate injuries, while the other was evaluated at the scene for minor injuries, according to a report from Newsbreak.
